content.text: Jira comments carry visibility {type, value} for role/group restriction, and JSM carries jsdPublic for internal-vs-customer-visible. gadak drops both on ingest and never sets them on write.

- internal/jira/types.go:42-48 (jira.Comment), internal/store/records.go:69-78 and the comments table in internal/store/schema.go:97-107 have no visibility or jsdPublic field. A grep for jsdPublic/visibility in product code returns nothing.
- internal/jira/write.go:110 AddComment sends the body only.

- Live mirror raw: jsdPublic true 5060, false 0 (search-inlined pages only — whether the paged comments table holds internal ones is unverified, because the struct drops the field before it reaches SQL).
- issuetap accepts a POST carrying visibility, answers 201, and the response has no visibility key. It is dropped silently on the origin side too.

This is not an ACL hole: Jira only returns comments the stored credential may see, so the mirror does not widen access. The defect is the missing marking. A restricted or internal comment appears in `gadak issue` and in SQL indistinguishable from a public one, so an agent summarising a ticket can republish it; and `gadak comment` is always public, so "leave this as an internal note" cannot be honoured.

Fix shape: comments.visibility_type / visibility_value and a nullable jsd_public (NULL = not a JSM comment); write flags (--visibility role=X, --internal). Then a line in the agent skill: filter on those before quoting a comment anywhere public. Mirror the origin's fields; do not build an ACL engine in gadak.
Gate: a fixture comment restricted to a role lands with a non-empty visibility column; a comment posted with --internal reads back the same; existing public comments stay NULL.
Found by the Jira-surface gap sweep (track B, score 8/10).
